Subject: Inference footprint review: 70B, 64k context, quantization options

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — we have an incoming Dedicated capacity discussion as part of our renewal/expansion (details in the HubSpot deal). Key asks from our infra and product teams:

- We plan to serve a 70B family model (weights compatible with Llama-style architectures).
- Typical inference pattern: streaming chat with long context (up to 64k tokens for a subset of customers).
- Target steady QPS: ~5 requests/sec, peak concurrency ~8 concurrent sessions during business hours.
- Latency SLO: ideally < 150ms per token for local turns; we can tolerate occasional token spikes.
- We are open to 4-bit/8-bit quantization, but product wants guidance on quality/latency trade-offs and concrete GPU counts for Dedicated pool sizing.

Can you provide a short advisory (GPU types, replica sizing, estimated memory footprint including KV cache for long context, and the practical savings from q4/q8)? We have some flexibility on budget but want a clear tradeoff matrix.

Thanks,
Paul

Hey team — I attached a short spreadsheet (novaedge_kv_profile.csv) and a one-pager (redwood_capacity_playbook_v2.pdf) with assumptions and calculations. Highlights below (TL;DR first):

TL;DR — Recommended starting configurations (tradeoff options):
- Option A (conservative, FP16 parity): 4 x H100-80GB GPUs per replica (model sharded across GPUs), supports 64k KV cache on-device with predictable latency. Best quality, highest cost.
- Option B (balanced, q4_0 quant + mixed precision KV): 2 x A100-80GB GPUs per replica with model quantized to 4-bit (weights) and KV kept fp16; reduces GPU memory needed for weights significantly while KV cache remains the dominant memory consumer for long contexts. Good cost/quality balance.
- Option C (aggressive cost-optimised): 1 x A100-80GB or L40S per replica using q4_0 + selective KV offload to host memory (RDMA-friendly setup). Lower cost but higher tail latency for large contexts. Use as burst/fallback option.

Primary assumptions used in calculations (short form):
- 70B model FP16 weights ~ 140 GB (70e9 * 2 bytes).
- q4_0 reduces weight footprint to ~35–40 GB (approx. 4-bit effective storage plus packing overhead).
- KV cache is proportional to context length and model hidden size; for a 64k context we estimate KV footprint in the range of 60–110 GB per concurrent session depending on whether KV is stored in fp16 (larger) or compressed (q8/q4 tokens).
- For your profile (QPS 5, peak concurrency 8): peak concurrent KV memory is the dominant driver. With 8 concurrent 64k sessions, on-device KV-only would be multiple hundreds of GBs unless using compression/eviction.

Concrete sample numbers (illustrative; see attached CSV for layer-by-layer):
- FP16 baseline (weights + KV on-device): weights 140 GB + KV ~ 80 GB = ~220 GB per replica. Requires multi-GPU sharding (e.g., 4 x 80GB H100 with NVLink/p2p).
- q4_0 weights + fp16 KV: weights ~40 GB + KV ~80 GB = ~120 GB. Fit across 2 x 80GB GPUs with careful placement (weight shards + KV distributed).
- q4_0 weights + compressed KV (q8/tokens) + KV partial host offload: weights ~40 GB + KV on-GPU avg ~30–50 GB = ~70–90 GB; feasible on a single 80GB GPU for one replica, but concurrent sessions require replicas or eviction.

Operational notes and recommendations:
- For long-context customers we recommend keeping KV on-device when low-latency is required. If you can accept slight p95 tail degradation, host-RDMA-backed KV offload can reduce GPU unit needs significantly.
- Start with Option B for most customers (2 x A100-80GB per replica), and enable canary fp16 replicas for the small set that requires strict parity.
- Autoscale by session (spin additional replicas when new long-context sessions are active); enforce a max-session-length policy for non-enterprise tiers to limit tail cost.
- Consider model distillation/long-context-aware adapters as a product path to lower KV footprint for the heaviest customers.

I put the layer-level memory breakdown and a few microbench results (q4_0 inference latency delta vs fp16 at short contexts) in the attached CSV and the PNG. Happy to walk through tomorrow.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Inference footprint review: 70B, 64k context, quantization options

Paul — quick answers and a concise procurement blurb below. Marissa attached measurements and I confirmed ops constraints with Dylan.

1) Replica count recommendation (steady-state):
- With Option B (2 x A100-80GB replicas): run 4 replicas. Rationale: 2 replicas handle steady QPS headroom (capacity planning for batching and background evictions); +1 for failover; +1 for canary/maintenance. This gives predictable capacity for QPS 5 and peak 8 concurrent sessions while allowing rolling upgrades.

2) Expected p95 token latency penalty for KV host-offload (Option C):
- Ballpark: additional 5–25 ms per token at p95 depending on host NIC (100Gbps+ RDMA) and whether KV is prefetching. In our microbench with q4 weights + partial KV offload we saw ~8–12 ms/token increase p95 for 32k contexts; worst-case with higher memory churn hit ~20–25 ms. That is often acceptable for batched/async use cases but can break tight streaming SLOs.

Procurement blurb (short):
"Redwood recommends a hybrid Dedicated pool to balance cost and latency. For NovaEdge's long-context 70B workload, a quantized baseline (q4_0) with 2 x A100-80GB replicas provides >40% reduction in GPU footprint versus fp16-only deployments while maintaining near-parity quality for most flows. We recommend 4 replicas in steady-state (2 active capacity + 2 for failover/canary) to meet the stated QPS and concurrency targets. For the subset of customers requiring strict fp16 parity, add 1–2 fp16 replicas (4 x H100 or equivalent) behind the routing policy to preserve UX while keeping costs contained."

Next steps: Dylan will draft a Dedicated capacity estimate (monthly committed units + burst) and we can attach this advisory to the HubSpot deal. Happy to set a 30-min call to walk procurement/security through the tradeoffs.

—Jonas
